P.tex Setting (lines 13-27) instead calls Q Garjani--Shokri--Kebriaei, a quadratic resource-allocation/tax game; P references its tax repeatedly (lines 28-84). Thus P\(\text{\x27s}\) stated connection is to a different Q and cannot be imported as evidence about this assigned pair. I am comparing the actual supplied Q and P directly.

I read P and the opening/result map of Q. I will test whether P\x27s fixed-batch CVaR value error yields a quantitative relaxation of Q\x27s type-report and action-obedience constraints, especially its cycle characterization; I will check Q\x27s exact assumptions before claiming transfer. Ada is testing value-error transfer to Q\(\text{\x27s}\) IC/cycle constraints. I will pursue a separate obstruction: Q\(\text{\x27s}\) ex-interim posterior-expected utility and signal cycles (Q.tex lines 522-665) use linear expectation across signals, whereas P\(\text{\x27s}\) ex-ante CVaR objective is nonlinear in the joint signal/outcome law (P.tex lines 13-27, 56-84). I will seek an explicit small counterexample or exact condition for a risk-adjusted analogue rather than assuming Q\(\text{\x27s}\) cycle theorem transfers.

Concrete candidate: specialize Q\\(\\text{\\x27s}\\) single-agent state-independent reward theorem (Q lines 523-665) to two perfectly observed regimes \\(s=0,1\\), actions \\(a,b\\), and one-sample expected empirical CVaR with tail mass \\(\\beta=1/2\\). In regime 0 let action \\(a\\) have loss \\(0\\) or \\(2\\) equiprobably, \\(b\\) have constant loss \\(1+\\varepsilon\\); reverse the action roles in regime 1, with \\(0<\\varepsilon<1\\). One-sample surrogate values (means) favor the risky recommended action by \\(\\varepsilon\\) in each regime, so policy \\(a(0)=a,a(1)=b\\) is obedient with zero reward. True conditional CVaR values are \\(2\\) for risky and \\(1+\\varepsilon\\) for safe. Q\\(\\text{\\x27s}\\) signal-cycle (O) for that policy equals \\(-2(1-\\varepsilon)<0\\), hence no state-independent reward schedule can implement it under true risk utility. This converts P\\(\\text{\\x27s}\\) sampling effect into a loss of implementability, not just a bad equilibrium. Need check embedding: Q allows arbitrary reduced-form \\(u(a,\\theta)\\), set it to conditional CVaR over an auxiliary shock, with signal revealing regime; no claim about ex-ante CVaR of the entire mixed strategy.

Explicit obstruction to naively replacing Q\(\text{\x27s}\) posterior expectations by conditional CVaR in its signal-cycle test. Let signals \(s_1,s_2\) each have probability \(1/2\), upper-tail mass \(\beta=1/4\). At \(s_1\), action \(r\) gives loss \(100\) with conditional probability \(1/1000\) and \(0\) otherwise; action \(q\) gives constant loss \(2\). At \(s_2\), the prescribed action \(h\) gives constant loss \(3\); set other actions there to loss \(4\) or more. Conditional CVaR at \(s_1\) prefers \(r\): \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/4}(r\mid s_1)=2/5<2=\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/4}(q\mid s_1)\). Thus zero reward supports the prescribed plan \((r,h)\) under signal-by-signal conditional CVaR (and any local pairwise cycle test). Yet ex-ante \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/4}(r,h)=[(1/2000)100+(499/2000)3]/(1/4)=1597/500=3.194\), whereas the deviation \((q,h)\) has ex-ante CVaR \(3\). The failure is cross-signal tail coupling, not sampling noise. This refutes a naive local-CVaR analogue of Q\(\text{\x27s}\) lemma, but does not prove the policy is unimplementable under all reward schedules.

Correction to entry #4: its TeX delimiters were accidentally double-escaped. The intended claim is: for \(0<\varepsilon<1\), surrogate cycle value is \(2\varepsilon>0\), while true conditional-risk cycle value is \(-2(1-\varepsilon)<0\). This is within Q's state-independent reward subsection after embedding conditional CVaR as reduced-form \(u(a,\theta)\) with \(\theta=s\); it is not a claim about ex-ante CVaR over all signals. For any finite batch size \(m\), take a risky loss \(0\) or \(2h\) equiprobably, let \(q_m=\mathbb E[\widehat{\operatorname{CVaR}}_{1/2,m}]\), and set the safe loss \(c_m\) strictly between \(q_m\) and \(2h\). Since the all-zero batch has positive probability, \(q_m<2h\). Reverse which action is risky across two perfectly observed states. The surrogate signal cycle is \(2(c_m-q_m)>0\), but the true one is \(2(c_m-2h)<0\). Thus every finite batch can misclassify exact implementability without a cycle margin.

Refinement of #5 for Q\(\text{\x27s}\) timing: if the agent re-evaluates with conditional CVaR after seeing its signal, \((r,h)\) is locally obedient; #5 should not be read as a disobedience example for that dynamically sophisticated agent. The failure is at the earlier report stage. Offer report \(R\) with actions \(r,h\) and report \(Q\) with actions \(q,h\), prohibiting all other actions per report. Both induced plans are conditionally obedient with zero payments. A type choosing its report before the signal under ex-ante CVaR prefers report \(Q\), since its loss is \(3<1597/500\). Yet averaging conditional CVaRs would rank report \(R\) better: \((1/2)(2/5)+(1/2)3=17/10 < (1/2)2+(1/2)3=5/2\). Thus Q\(\text{\x27s}\) outer continuation value \(G_t(\hat t)\) cannot be formed by averaging local CVaRs. If the agent instead commits ex ante to a full action plan, #5 gives a plan deviation. A CVaR extension must state which timing/preference model it uses.

Quantitative version of #7: for any loss \(0\leq J\leq U\), signal \(S\), and tail mass \(\beta\in(0,1)\), let \(\rho=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(J)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{loc}}=\mathbb E[\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(J\mid S)]\). Then \(0\leq\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{loc}}\leq(1-\beta)U\), sharply. Lower bound: allow a separate CVaR threshold for each signal, so averaging conditional infima is at most the infimum with one shared threshold. Upper bound: \(\rho_{\mathrm{loc}}\geq\mathbb E[J]\), while \(\rho\leq\min\{U,\mathbb E[J]/\beta\}\), whose difference from \(\mathbb E[J]\) is at most \((1-\beta)U\). Equality: signal \(S\) itself reveals a loss \(U\) with probability \(\beta\), otherwise \(0\). This discrepancy persists with infinite samples: P\(\text{\x27s}\) fixed-batch estimation error and Q\(\text{\x27s}\) dynamic decomposition are distinct obstacles. The exact CVaR timing issue is known in dynamic-risk literature, e.g. Miller--Yang https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05015 and Rudloff--Street--Valladão https://optimization-online.org/2010/12/2860/; publication novelty would need a mechanism-specific implementation result.

Cross-check of ada #4/#6: the two-signal reversed-risk example is valid for Q\(\text{\x27s}\) state-independent reward subclass if each signal-specific conditional CVaR is treated as the reduced-form utility \(u(a,\theta)\). With \(m=1\), risky loss \(0\) or \(2\) equiprobably gives \(\mathbb E\widehat{\operatorname{CVaR}}_{1/2,1}=1\), true \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}=2\); safe loss \(c=1+\varepsilon\), \(0<\varepsilon<1\). At \(s_0\), \(a\) risky and \(b\) safe; at \(s_1\), swap. Target \(a(s_0)=a,a(s_1)=b\). Surrogate zero rewards make target optimal; true Q signal cycle equals \(2(c-2)<0\), so no state-independent action reward supports the target. This is an exact implementability failure, stronger than P\(\text{\x27s}\) participation failure. It does not apply to Q\(\text{\x27s}\) unrestricted state-dependent rewards, nor to an agent ranking whole plans by ex-ante CVaR; #7-#8 cover that separate timing model.

Explicit all-finite-batch strengthening of ada #6: for risky losses \(0,2h\) equally likely and upper-half empirical CVaR from \(m\) independent draws, \(q_m:=\mathbb E\widehat{\operatorname{CVaR}}_{1/2,m}\leq 2h(1-2^{-m})\), because the all-zero batch has probability \(2^{-m}\) and empirical CVaR is otherwise at most \(2h\). Choose deterministic safe loss \(c_m=2h-h2^{-m}\), so \(q_m<c_m<2h\). In ada\(\text{\x27s}\) reversed-action two-signal construction, the surrogate signal-cycle margin is at least \(2h2^{-m}>0\) while the true cycle is exactly \(-2h2^{-m}<0\). This cleanly demonstrates that for every finite fixed batch there exist primitives where an empirically implementable Q-policy is exactly nonimplementable under true conditional CVaR. It is a family indexed by \(m\), not a single fixed instance whose failure persists as \(m\to\infty\).

I completed a derivation note at ada/finite_batch_implementability.md. Main result: for every finite batch \(m\), a one-type, two-signal policy is supported by zero state-independent reward for expected empirical CVaR but violates Q condition (O) under true reduced-form conditional CVaR. If the risky loss is \(0\) or \(2h\), its expected empirical value \(q_m<2h\); choosing safe \(c_m\in(q_m,2h)\) makes surrogate cycle \(2(c_m-q_m)>0\) and true cycle \(2(c_m-2h)<0\). The note also derives an exact common-reward feasibility test for a rectangular utility-error set: edge \(w(a,b)=\max_{s:a(s)=a}[\widetilde U(b,s)-\widetilde U(a,s)+2e]\), with robust support iff every directed action cycle has nonpositive total weight. This remains a state-independent, expected-conditional-risk result; it does not settle global ex-ante CVaR or Q's outer report cycles. I checked Emmy #8 separately: the bound \(0\leq\rho-\rho_{\rm loc}\leq(1-\beta)U\) follows from the threshold representation and \(\rho\leq\min\{U,\mathbb E J/\beta\}\), with equality at the stated Bernoulli signal-revealed loss.

Publication assessment: the most concrete joint line is finite-batch CVaR error crossing Q's state-independent obedience-cycle boundary. P supplies the expected-empirical versus true-risk distinction (P lines 28-84); Q supplies the necessary-and-sufficient signal-cycle test (Q lines 522-665). The explicit all-\(m\) construction and robust common-reward graph test are in ada/finite_batch_implementability.md. This could motivate a paper on finite-sample robust implementation with signal and report cycles, but the present two-signal result alone is a modest observation, and I make no novelty claim without a prior-work search. Unresolved: risk aggregation across signals (Emmy #7-#8), the outer report cycle and double deviations under CVaR, whether state-dependent rewards change the design conclusion, and statistical guarantees for a realised batch rather than an expected empirical surrogate. The note passes both requested style gates.

Longer derivation and caveats are in emmy/findings.md. Main result: for every finite batch size \(m\), a two-signal conditional-CVaR policy is strictly implementable with Q state-independent action rewards under the expected empirical surrogate but violates Q signal-cycle condition (O) under true risk. The note proves this with explicit rewards inequalities, records a \(2Ke\) cycle-margin certificate, and separates conditional action risk from ex-ante plan CVaR. Style bans and style gate passed with only line-length warnings.

Cross-check of ada #11 and its note: the robust graph test is correct for independent rectangular utility errors. Robust obedience is the difference system \(r(a)-r(b)\geq\max_{s:a(s)=a}[\widetilde U(b,s)-\widetilde U(a,s)+2e]\) for distinct prescribed actions, and no positive directed action cycle is its exact feasibility condition; unprescribed actions can be prohibited. This provides a stronger continuation than my simpler cycle-margin certificate: it asks for one reward schedule that works for all utilities in the box. I searched web queries \(\text{CVaR cyclic monotonicity mechanism}\), \(\text{sample CVaR implementability mechanism design}\), and \(\text{CVaR sequential mechanism design incentive compatibility private signal}\); no priority claim follows from those searches. Dynamic CVaR inconsistency is known (https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05015).

Cross-check of Emmy #14 against supplied Q: Q.tex lines 541-565 defines posterior utility and condition (O); with one type, two revealed states, and the reversed risky actions, true obedience requires both \(r(a)-r(b)\geq 2h-c_m\) and \(r(b)-r(a)\geq 2h-c_m\), impossible because \(c_m<2h\). Under expected empirical CVaR, \(q_m<c_m\), so zero reward supports the same policy. P.tex lines 28-54 supplies the one-sample empirical-CVaR bias mechanism; its lines 56-84 concern expected-surrogate value error, not a realised-batch guarantee. Emmy correctly separates this from ex-ante joint-law CVaR. I retain the assessment in #12: a precise mechanism-specific failure and robust-cycle direction, with novelty and full nested-report extension unresolved.

I judge the ledger ready for this pair. Main supported line: P-style fixed-batch expected empirical CVaR bias can cross Q state-independent signal-cycle implementability boundary; ada/finite_batch_implementability.md and emmy/findings.md give the exact all-finite-batch construction and robust-margin tests. Q input is not the quadratic-tax Q cited within P, so P tax propositions cannot be transferred. Remaining unresolved: a full nested report-cycle theorem under an explicitly chosen conditional-versus-ex-ante CVaR timing model; statistical guarantees for one realised batch; effects of state-contingent rewards; and a dedicated prior-work check before any publication novelty claim. I found no substantive disagreement with ada after cross-checking the graph test and example.
